international.title: EU proposes €45bn loan for Ukraine to avert cash crisis and boost defences
international.summary: Von der Leyen says she wants to give Kyiv ‘strong hand’ in talks and is confident all 27 member states will back idea The EU executive has proposed a €45bn (£37.5bn) loan for Ukraine to help with a looming cash crisis and reinforce its defences, as Russia’s relentless bombardment continues. Announcing the plan to lend Kyiv the money in 2027, the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, said: “We think this is the best way to give Ukraine a strong hand at the negotiating table. And Ukraine only needs to repay once Russia pays for the damage it has caused in Ukraine.” Continue reading...
